The KB entry pq_mass_density is the canonical record for mass density: symbol rho/ρ, definition 'Mass per unit volume', si_dimension 'M L^-3' (kg m^-3). That canonical record applies directly to the ledger variable because both the symbol and the physical definition match the ledger's wording and physical context (continuum/material density in laser melting). The pq_mass_density record therefore supports all nonzero coordinates in the proposed SI vector (mass exponent +1, length exponent -3) and the zeros for other base dimensions.

The ledger variable 'Tl-T0' is explicitly the temperature difference between melting and ambient temperatures. KB entry pq_temperature_difference records the canonical quantity 'temperature difference' with symbol forms including Tl-T0 and si_dimension 'Theta' (K). pq_thermodynamic_temperature is the canonical thermodynamic temperature record that further clarifies that differences of thermodynamic temperatures carry the same base-dimension Theta. Together these records directly justify the single nonzero Theta exponent and zeros elsewhere in the ledger vector: temperature difference has dimension Theta and no mass/length/time/current/amount dimensions.

The ledger names 'r0' as the laser beam radius, a geometric length. KB entry pq_laser_beam_radius is the curated canonical record for laser beam radius with si_dimension 'L' and symbol r0; pq_radius is the general radius/length record. Both records apply because the ledger variable is a geometric length scale (beam radius) used in laser-material interaction. These entries support the exponent L=+1 and zeros for all other base dimensions.

The ledger variable 'alpha' is defined as thermal diffusivity (thermal conductivity divided by density and heat capacity). KB entry pq_thermal_diffusivity is the canonical record for thermal diffusivity with si_dimension 'L^2 T^-1' (m^2 s^-1). This entry applies directly because the ledger text explicitly identifies alpha as the heat diffusivity used in heat transfer during laser melting; the pq_thermal_diffusivity record therefore supports L=+2, T=-1 and zeros for other base dimensions. (The KB also contains an alternate meaning 'thermal expansion coefficient' for the symbol alpha, but the ledger's definition removes that ambiguity.)

The ledger variable 'etaP' is described as effective absorbed laser power (laser power multiplied by absorptivity). The KB entry pq_effective_laser_power gives the canonical quantity 'effective absorbed laser power' (symbols etaP, P_abs) and records si_dimension 'M L^2 T^-3' (watts). The ledger's phrase that absorptivity is dimensionless aligns with the KB note that eta is dimensionless, so etaP has pure power dimensions. pq_effective_laser_power therefore supports M=+1, L=+2, T=-3 and zeros for other base dimensions.

The ledger defines 'cp' as specific heat capacity per unit mass. KB entries pq_specific_heat_capacity and pq_specific_heat_cp are the canonical records for specific heat (c_p) with si_dimension 'L^2 T^-2 Theta^-1' (J kg^-1 K^-1). These records apply because the ledger variable is the heat capacity per mass (isobaric specific heat), and they therefore support the nonzero exponents L=+2, T=-2, Theta=-1 and zeros elsewhere.

The ledger variable 'Vs' is the laser scan speed (linear velocity). KB entry pq_scan_speed is the canonical record for laser scan speed with si_dimension 'L T^-1' (m s^-1) and symbol Vs. Because the ledger variable is a velocity of the beam relative to the material, pq_scan_speed directly supports the exponents L=+1, T=-1 and zeros for other base dimensions.

Your reason must explain why each cited record applies to this variable in the original problem, not merely why its vector matches. If any current coordinate is unknown, request revision or report UNCERTAIN; never call a partly known vector PASSED. Give a complete correction when physically justified. If a correction remains partly unknown, preserve null and explain what remains unresolved; the program will request revision rather than invent zeros. Lack of KB alone is not a physical contradiction. Matrix compilation and n/r/k are program tasks, not audit tasks.
